overview.text: The Painted Bronzeback is a slender, harmless tree snake of South-east Asian forests.

identification.text: Olive or brown above with a yellow stripe along each side, edged below by a dark line; a black stripe through the eye.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Brunei, southern China, Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and Thailand. Populations from India, Bangladesh and Myanmar are now a separate species.

behaviour.text: Active by day and lives in trees. Special belly scales let it climb steep, smooth surfaces, and it can even 'jump' across gaps between branches.

recognise.text: Yellow side stripe on a bronze-brown body.
